Enigma

RuNyx

3.77
32,928 ratings5,967 reviews
Rate this book
A new breathtaking tale of unforgettable romance, set in a dark academia world of secret societies, lush suspense and sizzling sensuality, from RuNyx, the New York Times bestselling author of Gothikana.

Salem Salazar comes to Mortimer University to get to the bottom of her sister's mysterious death. There, obsessed with forensics, she discovers there have been a lot more unexplained deaths on the campus. Her search leads her down a dark and dangerous path to a secret society and to Caz.

Cazimir van der Waal is in her way and another mystery to unravel. Is he just an art student, a man living a double life, or a murderer? While also at the university seeking answers for another death, Caz has a lot more to him than meets the eye.

Secret forces are at play in Mortimer and no one is safe. As Salem tries to go under radar and Caz tries to block her path, somehow, they both end up in the crossfire of a powerful, secret society. They are forced to work together to discover the truth or risk losing their lives.

In this magnificent, steamy dark academia romance from RuNyx, sparks will fly, rivals will become lovers, and terrible secrets will be unleashed.

At the Publisher's request, this title is being sold without Digital Rights Management Software (DRM) applied.

"I own your mind. I'm going to own your body. And then, I'll take your soul. Because you're coming for mine, aren't you? Mind, body, and soul."

Oooh this is underrated. It made me relive that Nocticadia experience in a way. I loved the dark academia and goth vibes. The atmosphere was so intense and eerie, I was hooked from page one. And it wasn't even the romance (though that's always a plus) but I was mostly captivated by the murder mystery.

The murder mystery aspect is so well executed because it gives you just enough tidbits to keep you invested in the first half but it's almost that the lead isn't going anywhere. There are suspects but to theorize it, there isn't any concrete evidence until the second half when we finally really get to it. I loved how exceptionally well done that was to create that subtle yet intense allure.

Salem is a complex lead. She's definitely not for everyone. I won't lie she may read a bit bland on paper but there is depth to her. There's a subdued sort of emotional intensity to her that won't work for everyone. But she compliments Caz really well. I loved him so much. The bad boy energy is chef's kiss. I liked how he challenged her, pushed her, accepted her in all his possessive intensity. He's exactly the balance she needs to feel alive.

The romance between the two from rivals to lovers. The intense chemistry that clicks instantly yet takes a slow burning time to go anywhere had me melting. And the spice? Hot!!

The ending could have been better done though. That's the only reason it's not a five star for me. I feel like since 85% of the book had gone into resolving the murders and the secret society bits. There could have been more done with it. Subtle was fine. But I was looking for dramatic. A little bit more of action and more exposure would have solidified it for me but anyhoo, maybe that's just me.

Thanks to my girl Meg for reading this with me. I always have fun with you, babe.


~•~•~

Dark academia + secret societies? I NEED THIS!!

May 4, 2025
2.65 stars?
and trust me, that’s being generous. the only thing keeping me turning pages was Baron.

"Enigma" by RuNyx had me so hyped going in. The vibes? Immaculate. That dark academia aesthetic, the Hades x Persephone promise, the mystery, the forbidden obsession… like YES??? Inject that into my veins. But what I got? Felt like biting into a gooey-looking brownie only to realize it’s dry as hell on the inside.

Let’s start with the good (because there was some):

The chapter enders? Gorgeous. Every time I reached one, I had to stop and soak it in—highlighting, Googling, and falling down literary rabbit holes. They added this elegant, brainy touch to the story that I loved. And the atmosphere? Absolutely spellbinding. I swear I could feel the chill in the air, hear footsteps echoing in ancient corridors, and see candlelight dancing on the walls. If there's one thing RuNyx never misses, it's the vibe.

And Salem?
She was lowkey fascinating at first. Ice-cold, trauma-shielded, death-obsessed— I was INTO IT. She had that hot girl tragic energy I live for. But then she just… fizzled.
Like, after the halfway point she lost her flavor. She went from mysterious loner to basic heroine real quick. Girl went from "I don’t need anyone" to "Caz plz ruin me" in one sec?? Not buying it.

Caz?
Listen. I usually live for the broken artist archetype. Dark eyes, haunted soul, fingers stained with paint and grief? That should’ve worked. But hot?? Eh. Interesting? Kinda. Swoon-worthy? Not even close. He had angst, sure, but not the kind that makes you spiral or write midnight fanfic. Just… mid.

The romance was such a letdown. There were crumbs of chemistry at the start—banter that had potential, lingering glances that hinted at tension. But then it just… vanished. Once they got together, there was no build, no fire, no angst, no tension —nothing. It felt like insta-lust disguised as deep emotional connection and I HATE that. One minute she’s dead-eyed and numb, next minute she’s thirsting over him like it’s Wattpad. Make it make sense.
Also, the sex scenes? Felt forced. Not RuNyx hot. More like "I guess we’re doing this now???" shrug

Now, the plot. oh boy.
Started off like a thriller. I was intrigued. I was INVESTED.
And then? Chaos. Just pure chaos. It tried juggling secret societies, missing girls, art, trauma, generational wealth, cults, romance, existential dread— like slow down. There’s only so many things I can track at once. By the end, it was just info-dump after info-dump, every big twist crammed into like ten pages, and I was exhausted. That final secret society showdown?? Embarrassing. No buildup. No emotional payoff. Just… okay, guess that’s over now.

I wanted chills. I wanted obsession. I wanted a love story so intense it hurt. Instead I got a Pinterest board with dialogue.

I’m not saying it was awful. The writing? Still solid. The vibe? Top tier. Baron? Give that man a book immediately.
But Enigma didn’t grip me. It didn’t shake me.
And for RuNyx? That’s just disappointing.

Final thoughts?
Atmosphere carried.
Salem had promise.
Baron is the ✨moment.✨
But Caz didn’t deliver, the romance flopped, and the plot fell apart.
Would I read the next book? Maybe. Out of loyalty. But only if Baron’s the star.

2.65/5
And that’s me being nice.

June 20, 2025
❝ she had looked like a goddess, a mystical creature hovering over the dead, come to life from the sea behind her. and in that one instant, she had become his muse. ❞


‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ enigma is a novel that tries so hard to be cryptic and clever that it looped all the way back around to feeling like one long loading screen. i flipped to the very end, hoping i’d vanish like the victims too, but no, i was still there, tragically conscious. my most powerful act of empathy in this whole book was toward the dead people, because at least they got to leave.


₊˚꒰ 𖧷 ꒱ ⊹ i. plot. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ so, remember the secret history by donna tartt? this book clearly does. it tosses us into a mysterious elite college that practically acts like a cult with missing sisters, suspicious professors, and murder. except, nothing ever happens!

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ salem salazar arrives at mortimer university, all bright-eyed, trauma-trained, and armed with a single brain cell, to investigate why her sister kicked the bucket. at mortimer, rich kids are being elitist and useless, there are secret societies that potentially murder people, and students who literally throw themselves off a cliff. enter cazimir van der waal, a tall, broody, mysterious dreamboat with the emotional intelligence of a traffic cone and the bland personality of plain oatmeal. he materializes from the shadows to say one unsettling thing, then despawns.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ you’d think all this would build toward a thrilling conspiracy with twists and danger. hilarious of us, truly. instead, we get 400+ pages of vibes, vibes, and hallway conversations. the "grand mystery" gets solved in about two paragraphs, like the author suddenly remembered, mid-sentence, "oh shit, the plot." this book had no business being over 400 pages. the actual storyline could’ve fit on a well-organized post-it note.


₊˚꒰ 𖧷 ꒱ ⊹ ii. writing. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ runyx can write. that's not in question. there are lines here that are objectively pretty, the kind of thing you'd highlight and post on pinterest with a blurry forest background. the problem is that every sentence wants to be that sentence. there’s no off switch. it's like being stuck at a party with someone who speaks exclusively in poetic monologues. halfway through a paragraph i'd realize i’d forgotten where we are, what we’re talking about, and whether i paid my power bill.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ and then, just when you're adjusting to the moody gothic prose setting, someone opens their mouth and goes, "he's such a hunky chonk of a man! like who's this brooding beefcake?" i had to put the book down and stare at the wall. deeply unsettling jump scare. imagine building this whole spooky, atmospheric, culty campus and then hitting me with hunky chonk brooding beefcake. this is not banter. this is a war crime.


₊˚꒰ 𖧷 ꒱ ⊹ iii. romance and characters. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ salem and caz’s connection feels less like a love story and more like a long, drawn-out hostage negotiation. they bond over what, exactly? trauma? vibes? mutual proximity to cliffs? caz is marketed as this dangerous, obsessive, morally gray man, but half the time he just reads like the guy your friends warn you about and you date anyway because you love red flags and bad decisions. and salem, my girl, keeps insisting she’s not into murder and mayhem while simultaneously getting hot and bothered whenever he looks at her like a puzzle he could dismember.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ nothing screams romance like the man getting turned on by your panic attacks and pins you to the wall while you’re having one. the fact that everyone acts like this is normal and not a very urgent reason to block his number and move countries is insane. "morally gray" has packed her bags and left the building. this is just concerning.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ the side characters blur together into one amorphous blob of enigmatic college people with trauma. honestly, the missing sister had more presence than half the actual cast, and she’s dead in chapter zero.


₊˚꒰ 𖧷 ꒱ ⊹ iv. conclusion. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ listen, i'll give the book this. the aesthetic and vibes are immaculate, but i was promised a mystery and not 400 pages of nothing.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ this book made me so annoyed i slammed out this review in fifteen minutes powered entirely by spite and disappointment. i’ll probably come back to edit once i’m less homicidal about wasted potential.

— 1.5 stars. ⋆˚☆˖°.ᐟ

Oh boy. This was rough. There’s some fun going in, but once you’re inside… it’s just a whole lot of nothing. It’s like being promised a rollercoaster and ending up on one of those sad mall trains that goes two miles an hour.

The unnecessary in-depth details were a full-on sensory attack. And the mmc? Why does he sound like a predator lurking in plain sight? I was less worried about romance and more worried about filing a missing person report.

This is my second book from this author and at this point I think it’s time for us to see other people. My first thought after finishing was “I’M FREEEEE.” Picture me running through a field, arms wide, screaming with joy. This book may have taken hours of my life, but at least now I can frolic in peace.

Enigma — noun:
A person or thing that is mysterious, puzzling, or difficult to understand… and this book is exactly that in the best way possible. 🖤🌫️

This dark academia, gothic romance checked all my favorite boxes:

— Murder Mystery 🗡️
— Dark Coastal Setting 🌊
— Found Family vibes 🖤
— Secret Societies and Dangerous Games ⏳
— An Elite, Old University 🏰
— Rivals to Lovers tension so thick you could cut it with a knife ⚔️
— Push/Pull Dynamic: She’s Ice, He’s Fire ❄️🔥
— Possessive of each other in the best way 🖤
— Public Claims… swoon 🥵
— Mysterious Artist MMC + Morbid Criminology-Obsessed FMC 🎨🔬
— High Stakes & Constant Danger lurking around every corner ⚠️💀

Salem and Caz were pure magic together. She’s always been invisible — overlooked, cast aside by her family and the world — until him. The way he truly sees her, even in the quietest moments, had me in my feels. 🥹

Their connection was intense, addictive, and full of that delicious angst I crave. They try to stay away… but fate (and obsession) had other plans.✨

The high stakes, constant danger, and secret society tension kept me flipping the pages, and the dark, misty vibes pulled me all the way in.❤️‍🔥

This one gave me all the gothic feels I loved from Gothikana — but honestly? Even better. If you’re into secret societies, twisted romance, and characters who were absolutely made for each other, Enigma will own you. 🖤

✮⋆˙You give me a modicum of peace in a world of chaos✮⋆˙

Mother Ru has done it again! Gosh, I adore her writing style so much and this didn't let me down! Dark academic romance is one of my favourite genres and this eerie and gothic atmosphere was perfect for it, paired with her beautifully descriptive story telling, I felt like I was right at Mortimer. 

The plot was on point! Expect an dark and misty academic setting with lot of mystery, secret societies, steamy romance, rivals to lovers with lots of tension, a possessive MMC (🤭), strong female friendships & lots of second guessing yourself!

Firstly, Salem, I adored as an FMC. She is different but fascinating. She isn't in your face but her presence is so loud throughout this story, the way she holds herself and doesn't shy away from being herself. Understanding her struggles growing up, through not being accepted due to her own fascinations that are out of the ordinary in a well to do society, mixed in with her grief and feeling of having no one stay for her. Then seeing her being loved unapologetically by multiple people, she deserves it all. 

Caz, obviously I am obsessed with him. The enigma. The voice of rumbling seas and raspy smoke. He takes possessive and runs with it and I love me a fictional man who is so disgustingly possessive he looses his mind when another man so much as looks at his girl. Not to mention he is down so bad for her. Touch her and die will literally never get old. Of course we want him threatening people over her, of course! 

"I want to be the only villain you see. I want to be the only devil who drags you to hell."

The romance, I was sat and seated for Salem and Caz. The way the complimented each other so well, not to mention the tension and the angst was, chefs kiss. They aren't my favourite Ru couple but she still knows how to write romance beautifully, every time she draws me into the most epic love stories. 

'Maybe they were both the poison. Maybe they were both the antidote. Maybe what they thought would infect them was going to cure them after all'.

As much as I loved this book, I will say it was on track to be a 5 star read, however; I felt the ending and finding out the truths was wrapped up so quickly! After such a enthralling story, I just wish we had spent a bit more with the Salem and Caz in the aftermath, rather than jumping straight to the epilogues. Therefore I felt my rating drop towards the end.
I would be down bad for a Baron book!! 

Favourite Quotes:
"She might not know anything else about him, but she knew that he hasn't left her alone when he had all the reasons to, and that was enough for now."

"Because I was a man on the path to damnation and I saw salvation instead. Because being near you make me feel something beyond rage. Because the chaos inside me quietens when I'm near you" 

"Because life with you feels greater than death"

"Salem always thought nothing could beat death, that nothing could be immortal. She'd been wrong. Love, deep, true love, was immortal"

Rating: 3 stars.
So I was giving this book a 4 stars cause it is good but after thinking a lot, I was just like meh…yeah it was mid.

I went into this book with such high hopes because the setup was so good creepy atmosphere, twists that actually had me second-guessing myself, and that delicious sense of “something big is about to happen.” For a while, it really felt like it was building toward something epic. But then… it just didn’t deliver. The pacing dragged, and when things finally did start to happen, it was messy instead of thrilling. The plot threads felt scattered, like the author threw too many ideas at the wall and didn’t tie them together. And that ending? Brutal in the worst way. Rushed, anticlimactic, and lacking any real payoff. What could have been a jaw-dropping finale ended up leaving me frustrated and unsatisfied.

➛ Salem:
Salem had me in the palm of her hand at the start. Cold, mysterious, trauma-wrapped, death 'obsessed' she was giving me everything I wanted in a heroine. I loved how unapologetically sharp she was, like she didn’t need to be palatable for anyone. But somewhere around the halfway mark… it was like a switch flipped. The moment she got with the MMC, all that sharpness dulled. She slipped into this generic, watered-down role, and it hurt because the version of her I met at the beginning felt so powerful and unique.

➛ Caz:
And then there’s Caz. Dark, tortured, broody artist with that obsessive streak—on paper, he should’ve destroyed me. That’s literally my kryptonite. But instead of slow-burn obsession that simmers, his fixation on Salem just hit out of nowhere and way too hard. His potential was right there, but without more depth and history to his character, it felt surface-level.

As for the romance… oof. Those first crumbs of chemistry? GOLD. The banter, the subtle glances, the quiet tension, it had me ready for a feast. But instead, the tension evaporated the second they got together. No build-up, no angst, no fire, just insta-lust disguised as some kind of deep connection. Honestly, it left me questioning if Salem even knew Caz at all. What could’ve been electric fizzled into something flat and forgettable.




“Every hallway whispers, every locked door hides a sin, and every kiss feels like a warning.”
⋆.˚☁️⋆ Honestly, I’ve had my eye on this book for what feels like forever, but for some reason I just never picked it up. Now that I’m finally here, I’m kind of hyping myself up while also side-eyeing all those one and two star ratings everyone keeps giving it. Like…I want to be excited, and I am, but not as much as I thought I’d be. It’s giving cautious optimism vibes that I’m ready to dive in.
But I’m bracing myself just in case it doesn’t live up to the dark, twisty potential I’ve been imagining.

The Vibes?
dark secrets with twisted romance.

Fascinated by death, Salem has always been drawn to the dark things others avoid. But when death begins to follow her, leaving behind more than just questions, her obsession turns into something far more dangerous.

Now that she's a student at Mortimer University, an elite school shrouded in legacy, secrets, and shadows. Salem is pulled into a mystery buried deep in its past. Yet as she searches for answers, she must decide: will uncovering the truth save her, or lead her to her own grave?

⊹ ࣪ ˖ੈ Characters

⟡ Salem Salazar - she is peculiar and fascinated with death. Most would call her weird, icy, and stoic, yet she has more to her than what she lets out. She is intelligent, overly curious, and will always see to it that whatever crosses her mind finds its answers (but it would take the whole book before she does, cause she needs to satisfy her curiosity about Caz before all the mystery surrounding Mortimer). Salem has gorgeous curls and curves that will be stated many times in the story.

I fear this will be a hate review with the emotions Cora and I had reading this. If you loved Enigma, this probably isn’t the review for you. So, please consider clicking away. Thank you!

I love a good atmospheric book. It's often the deciding factor in how much I enjoy a story. In the beginning, Enigma’s writing and world-building hooked me in, but to make a book all mysterious and shadowy to the point that it fogs the whole plot of the story just made me question if the mystery was even relevant to begin with. The mystery didn’t deepen; it just blurred into obscurity. Because what do you mean we were already 70-80% in the book, yet the overall mystery felt like a pimple inside your nostril (it’s there and it's bothering you, you can feel it but can’t see it, and you just want to pop it and move on). And that reveal? wth was that? It felt like a random weekend night that ended just cause an uninvited guest entered the venue.

Now onto the characters, who unfortunately had all the depth of a shadow, no chemistry, and had the most random lore/back stories. Don’t get me wrong, I genuinely liked Salem and was fascinated with her in the beginning, but it slowly took a turn when she prioritized her curiosity with Caz more than finding out the haunting that Mortimer has (mind you, she was obsessed with solving the school's mystery for half of her life, then magically, she sees Caz, and now he has become the only thing orbiting around her brain. I was intrigued by the obsession and possessiveness connection they had, and I wanted a deeper exploration of it. Unfortunately, it just gave us more spice scenes and a reveal that made you think they had a deeper history.

❝ Death still was inevitable, but life was more beautiful somehow because of it. ❞


Honestly, this could go on longer, but I'm just going to cut it short. All I can say is that this would have been a 0-star if not for the gothic and eerie build-up of Mortimer. Other than that, it was disappointing to read. I had high hopes, especially as a fan of the Dark Verse series. I was sure this would be the one because it had everything that I wanted (gothic vibes, dark academia, mystery, and romance). But lo and behold, it did not. Nonetheless, thank you for the atmospheric writing, good start, and gothic vibes. 1-star for that.

It’s a RuNyx book, so the review won’t be short by any means, even if I can just go ahead and tell you:
“A Caz art masterpiece wrapped in Salem’s skymind, written in soul, poetry, and an abyss of echoes and feelings. All threaded with mystery, chemistry, and meaning.” – Grace, an undone reader
But I can’t just tell you that now, can I?
So here are my thoughts:

⭐Rating
My heart says 5 stars. My gut says 4.5. It feels unfair to go lower when so much care, grief, and art were poured into this story.
Yes, I had questions. Yes, I needed more closure.
But yes, I felt this story in my bones.
Sometimes we have to find closure in the unknown, and that’s something RuNyx taught us with Morana and in Gothikana, specifically.
So I’ll meet myself halfway and say:
RuNyx gave us a book that speaks to grief, chemistry, chaos, and the quiet act of choosing to live.
It’s not perfect. But it’s sacred.

🖤 Voice of Smoke and Sea
No one writes voices like RuNyx. She should seriously get an award just for that.
I could hear Caz before he even spoke, and it did something to my insides.
The audiobook as a whole was a perfect vessel for Enigma.
Jaclyn Kelso, the narrator, was incredible. She embodied Salem so well, her male voice was chef’s kiss, and while I do wish we had a duet narration, her performance helped me savour this world and transported me there.
Aiden Snow did not miss either; he delivered on the voice of smoke and sea, and goodness, it was like a balm for my soul.

🧬 The alchemy of RuNyx’s love stories
The romance in Enigma isn't just chemistry—it’s alchemy.
RuNyx lovers aren’t just written to fall for each other. They’re already connected. By something deeper. Threaded together by a kind of chemistry that feels fated, electric, ancient. The silent communication, the mirrored wavelengths, the magnetic pull that exists before a word is spoken.
And yes, for some readers, it might feel like insta-love, but for those who really look, it’s two souls whose lives have been quietly moving toward one another, until they collide and recognise each other at the precise moment they’re most needed.
This isn’t sudden—it’s inevitable, just like death. And it becomes immortal and immortalised.
The way Caz and Salem orbit each other? The kind of love Ru writes about teaches us that love can be silent, wordless, and still louder than anything else. Runyx’s characters don’t need to say “I love you” for you to feel it.
It teaches something powerful: that love can be known without words, understood in a glance, and felt in the marrow.
It invites us—old and new generations alike—to unlearn narrow definitions of love and open ourselves to something deeper, truer, wilder.

⚰️ Life, Death, and the Art of Breathing
RuNyx writes contrasts like no other. The way death and life interweave from morbid curiosity and an inevitability, to the act of coming alive and living life despite that is to be studied.
Death in Enigma makes me feel like I want to live life where I can meet mine with a smile, whether it will be a star in the sky or a simple biological equation.
The story doesn’t shy away from grief, loss, or the painful silence between family members. Knowing that RuNyx wrote this while grieving her own mother makes this narrative even more powerful. It’s catharsis on paper. And I genuinely feel privileged to be able to read this and for her to share it with us.
We saw Salem’s forensic brain at the start, sharp and curious. While it did fade into the emotional arc later on, I loved that shift—it marked her growth. Loneliness, which was once a loud ache, became an old friend, and Salem made new and “present” ones.

🖋️ Writing and Storytelling
Here’s the deal—I usually take RuNyx books for what they intend to be, and Enigma is, at its core, a story about loneliness and understanding death. For that? It’s a 5-star book.
However, there are questions left open. I was okay with not knowing everything, but I needed a few more crumbs about some main plot threads. 🌀
But,
RuNyx doesn’t spoon-feed her readers. She writes like someone who knows every detail in the back of her mind (because, duh, she does) but chooses to give us only what the MC know or how they process the world and things around them. I love this. Her writing shifts based on whose POV we’re in, proof of her brilliance.
💫And, every time she drops a Ru-verse mention, my heart grows a little and does a happy dance. I felt like we were being gifted little Easter eggs. 💫

🔎What I need more of:
I mean, if RuNyx blesses us with all of this? Yes, please.
• More Caz. RuNyx men are so complex and deep, and her love of psychology shines in them, and I need everything.
• A longer fallout arc – the behind-the-scenes and the aftermath (the answers to some of my questions)
• More Caz-Baron interactions
